scope: Passive public-source adoption assessment. No public swarm joined; no inference requested from third parties.
assessment: Independent reports establish some P2P and RPC sharding use. Public evidence does not establish widespread deployment, current large public swarms, or a distributed-user count. The managed NATS/PostgreSQL mode has separate recent deployment evidence.
count_limitations: Keyword matches overlap, include proposals/security reports and incidental mentions, and miss alternate wording. They are not numbers of users, successful deployments, or active peers. The initial P2P response had only 15 items; p2p_issue_mentions_all contains all 20 returned results.

evidence.finding: A user describes a working heterogeneous ARM/x86 CPU setup with two workers, while reporting a thread-count limit. Historical self-report, not a present-day deployment census.

Independent Kubernetes example uses a shared P2P token and three RPC workers, with GPU memory output after inference. Workers use A100 MIG partitions; this is not evidence of three distinct physical machines or a WAN swarm.
Independent compose stack includes a P2P worker setup and reports prior success. Its author later reports a regression in issue 3968. This is historical implementation/use evidence.
GPU user attempts P2P worker installation, reporting a missing backend. Evidence of demand/attempts rather than completed inference.

evidence.mode: RPC sharding; P2P discovery not established
evidence.finding: A user reports distributed inference working in Kubernetes with five Vulkan GPU workers after pinning the backend version. The report does not establish P2P discovery, internet operation, or ongoing production use.
Operator reports two registered compute nodes and successful scheduling/inference behind a lightweight frontend. This mode is distinct from P2P sharding.
P2P settings race fix in pinned local history. A maintenance signal, not a deployment count.
Two voluntary named production entries; neither description claims P2P sharding. Non-exhaustive list cannot establish zero distributed production users.
Official explorer root and /networks returned HTTP 521 in earlier local probes. Public population remains unknown, not zero.

official_positioning: Docs place P2P under ad-hoc/community/experimentation and managed NATS/PostgreSQL under production infrastructure. Positioning is not adoption evidence.

adopters_snapshot:
# Adopters

Organisations running LocalAI, listed by the people who run it.

If your organisation uses LocalAI and you are happy to say so publicly, open a
pull request adding a row to the table below. That pull request is how we know
we have permission to list you, which is why we do not add anybody ourselves.

You do not need to be a large company, and you do not need to disclose anything
sensitive. A sentence on what you use it for is more useful to other readers
than a logo.

## How to add yourself

1. Add a row to the table, in alphabetical order.
2. Use your organisation's usual name and a link to your site.
3. Say briefly what you use LocalAI for, and whether it is in production.
4. Open the pull request from an account that makes it plausible you speak for
   the organisation, or say in the description who you are. We may ask.

To be removed, open a pull request deleting your row, or email
[info@localai.io](mailto:info@localai.io). We will not ask why.

## Who is using LocalAI

<!-- Keep alphabetical. Columns: Organisation | What for | Status -->

| Organisation | What they use it for | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [solstone](https://solstone.app) | Runs [parakeet.cpp](https://github.com/mudler/parakeet.cpp) on-device as our speech-to-text server. | Production |
| [walcz.de](https://walcz.de) | Self-hosted appliance for a German B2B consultancy: local-only inference on AMD Strix Halo (gfx1151/ROCm), agents with MCP tools, RAG over an internal knowledge base, and a document/bookkeeping pipeline. | Production |
| _Your organisation here_ | | |

## What this list is not

This is not a list of everyone who has ever starred the repository, and it is
not a list of the employers of people who have contributed a patch. Both of
those are easy to scrape and neither means what a logo wall implies.

The website shows two separate things, both of which are checkable without
anybody's permission:

- **Engineers from these companies have contributed code.** Evidence is the
  commit history plus the employer on that person's public GitHub profile. It
  is a claim about a person, not about their employer.
- **These projects integrate LocalAI.** Evidence is a reference to LocalAI in
  that project's own repository or documentation.

Those two lists live in [`website/data/ecosystem.yaml`](website/data/ecosystem.yaml).
This file is the third, stronger thing: organisations that chose to say so.

research_implication: A bounded local security study is justified by actual feature use and maintained code. Claims of high deployment impact need more operator evidence, or a finding that generalizes to shared components such as llama.cpp RPC or EdgeVPN.
